newsitem.title: USA: Anheuer-Busch posts higher second-quarter net, sales.
newsitem.headline: Anheuer-Busch posts higher second-quarter net, sales.

text.p: Anheuser-Busch Cos. Inc., the world's largest beer brewer, said Wednesday it earned $381 million, an increase of 8 percent from its year-earlier operating income.
Anheuser, whose beer brands include Budweiser and Bud Light, said its U.S. market share remained at 44.3 percent in the first half of the year, essentially unchanged from a year ago.
While competitive pricing has put a lid on Anheuser's market share and sales growth in the United States, the St. Louis-based brewer said it expects its market share to edge higher for all of 1997.

"We expect to have a modest share increase for the year, W. Randolph "Randy" Baker, chief financial officer, said in a telephone interview. "We are seeing some improvements in sales trends now that we are positioned competitively."
Anheuser ended 1996 with a 45.2 percent market share.
Company officials said market share varies between quarters and comparisons are made between comparable periods.
Anheuser said it earned $381.2 million, or 76 cents a share. A year earlier, the company earned $353.4 million, or 70 cents a share from continuing operations.
Including a gain related to an earlier sale of food businesses, Anheuser earned 387.2 million, or 78 cents a share, in the same period of 1996.
Second-quarter net sales, which exclude excise tax on beer, were $2.99 billion, up 1.1 percent from $2.96 billion a year ago.
Anheuser said competitive pricing in the United States hurt its domestic beer volume growth, which rose only 0.8 percent in the second quarter to 23.8 million barrels.
The company's worldwide volume edged up 0.8 percent to 25.6 million barrels in the second quarter, including a 1.2 percent gain in international sales to 1.8 million barrels.

Anheuser said competitive pricing will trim the growth in its earnings per share for all of 1997, which is now expected to be in line with the 8.5 percent posted in the first half of 1997. That is below its stated goal of double-digit annual earnings increases.

"...(G)iven the current pricing environment, we now expect earnings per share growth for the full year to be consistent with year-to-date results, slightly below our long-term growth objective," company Chairman August Busch III said in a statement.
Baker added, however, the Anheuser's long-term earnings growth goal has not changed.
"We reaffirmed our long-term objective," he said. "We believe that the activitites in the market place are of a short-term nature."
He added that competitive pricing and promotions by other brewers are not a "sustainable strategy."

Anheuser also said its total international beer volume growth was led by significant volume expansion in the United Kingdom and China. Strong volume growth in China has led to the expansion of the Wuhan brewery, which is expected to be complete in 1998 and will double the plant's capacity to 2.1 million barrels.
Anheuser shares closed at $45.25, down $2.625, in composite New York Stock Exchange trading.
